transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-02-12
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Elena Ruiz (Redwood SE), Jonah Yu (Redwood SRE), Priya Menon (Orion Head of ML), Marco Alvarez (Orion Infra Lead), Tess Barton (Orion Security), Ethan Cole (Orion GPU Ops), Liu Zhao (Orion Data Eng)

Summary (auto): Quick technical deep dive focused on air-gapped/offline deployment logistics: delivery mechanisms for artifacts, offline licensing activation, GPU driver compatibility and pinned kernel modules, and verifying inference runtime optimizations (KV cache, batching, quantization) in an on-prem context. Agreed next steps include delivery of an offline artifact bundle, target host inventory, and scheduling a 48-hour benchmark run.

Topics:
- Offline artifact packaging (tarball vs OCI save)
- Offline license tokens and signed entitlements
- GPU driver versions, signatures, and vendor (NVIDIA vs AMD/ROCm) support
- Runtime kernel selection, quantization caveats on non-NVIDIA hardware
- KV cache warm-start and persistence for cold starts
- Batching/autoscale constraints in air-gapped environments

Transcript:
00:00 Samir: hey everyone thanks for making time, um I'm going to kick us off. we scheduled 60 minutes but i expect we might run a few over, okay?
00:12 Priya: yes, that's fine. thanks, Samir. we're mostly here to nail down the artifact delivery and licensing model for the on-prem rollout.
00:24 Marco: and driver compatibility — we have mixed GPU types across our clusters, so we need clarity on what you support.
00:33 Elena: totally. we'll cover supported GPU families and then the offline packaging options. quick intro — I'm Elena on the runtime team, focus on kernel selection and quantization.
00:44 Ethan: hi, I'm Ethan. i'm the gpu ops person, i'll be doing the installs. i'll add that we run RHEL 8.6 on most hosts and some Ubuntu 22.04 in our dev ring.
00:55 Jonah: Jonah here, Redwood SRE — i'll own the artifact delivery pipeline from our side and help with checksums/signing.
01:06 Tess: tess from security — we'll want the offline activation flow for licensing to be auditable and not require inbound access from the air-gapped network.
01:17 Samir: understood. let's start with the packaging options. Elena?
01:22 Elena: yes. we generally offer two artifacts for air-gapped customers: a) a tarball that contains the runtime binary, the model bundle in sharded format, precompiled kernels for specific GPU families, an offline OCI index (docker save tar) of our base image plus envs, plus checksums and a short install script; b) an encrypted installer image that comes with an offline license token that the installer validates locally.
01:48 Priya: can you clarify the 'precompiled kernels' bit? our infra team is cautious about running out-of-tree modules.
01:56 Elena: right. those are JIT/compiled kernels tuned per arch and per cuda/cudnn version — we ship multiple kernel variants, e.g., for CUDA 11.8+ with cuDNN 8.x, and for ROCm 5.x for AMD. if we don't have an exact match, the runtime will fall back to a portable path which is slower but functional.
02:16 Marco: how big are these tarballs? we have limited SFTP windows for transfers.
02:22 Elena: the full bundle with models ~ 35-45GB depending on model size; base runtime and kernels about 1.2-3GB. we can do a split bundle or delta bundles based on what you already have.
02:34 Marco: split is preferable. we can SCP in chunks or use a physical USB transfer if needed.
02:40 Samir: note — we'll provide sha256 checksums and signed manifests; Jonah will walk through signing.
02:47 Jonah: yes, manifests will be signed with our code-signing key; we'll also provide a PGP-signed manifest if your security team prefers that.
02:56 Tess: good. on licensing — what does offline activation look like? we don't want any calls to redwood.com from the air-gapped network.
03:06 Samir: we've got two flavors: time-limited offline tokens and perpetual entitlements. the offline token flow is: you run the installer, it generates a CSR-like activation request (hash of install environment + hwid), you transfer that request out of the air-gapped environment via a secure jump host or USB, we sign it server-side and return a signed token which you then apply locally. no inbound connections required.
03:35 Tess: and the signing key stays with Redwood? what's the audit trail?
03:40 Samir: yes, signing keys remain in our HSM. we issue signed tokens that include expiry, entitlements, and a signature. we also produce a verification manifest and log an issuance event to the account. you'll get a signed copy for your records.
03:52 Tess: sounds reasonable. any way to do on-site activation if you folks prefer?
03:56 Samir: we can support a temporary VPN tunnel or proxy if both sides agree, but many customers prefer the offline signed token flow for compliance.
04:06 Priya: license revocation? in case we need to remove access quickly.
04:10 Samir: revocation is handled server-side by blacklisting tokens — if you create a new token it will replace the previous except if the previous is perpetual then we need to coordinate. for emergency revocation, we'd ask you to zero the license file locally; we'll support an out-of-band revocation manifest you can apply.
04:25 Marco: back to drivers — we run a mix: A100s in our training pool, RTX6000s on inference, and a small set of MI250s. do you support ROCm for the MI250s?
04:38 Elena: yes, ROCm 5.x line is supported, but we do not yet have the same kernel-optimized paths as our CUDA path. quantized int8 kernels are more mature on CUDA; ROCm will use the portable kernels and may have some perf delta. we'll provide guidance on batch sizes to approximate throughput.
05:00 Ethan: driver installation policy — our cluster policy refuses unsigned kernel modules. do your runtime drivers require unsigned modules?
05:08 Elena: we avoid out-of-tree kernel modules generally; our approach is user-space runtime with optional kernel-level helpers for tiny latency gains. for the NVIDIA stack we rely on NVIDIA's signed drivers. for anything that would need a kernel module we can provide signed modules where possible, and instructions for verifying signatures.
05:26 Liu: what about container runtimes? we run containerd with gVisor for some workloads. offline images to import: will the docker save include the nvidia/cuda layers?
05:37 Jonah: yes, the offline OCI image tar includes all layers we control; note though NVIDIA's proprietary layers are not redistributed — we provide a stub or pointer and you must bring the driver package. we can provide an image with the runtime userland but it will expect the host driver to be installed.
05:55 Marco: okay. we need a concrete checklist of host-level pre-reqs.
05:59 Elena: we'll include a host checklist: kernel version ranges, required packages (glibc version, python3), recommended cgroups config, ulimit and hugepages notes, and GPU driver versions tested.
06:14 Tess: audit logging — will the installer write an install log and an activation record? we need those for SOC2 evidence.
06:21 Samir: yes, installer emits an installation manifest JSON and a separate activation record; both are signed and you can ship copies to your audit repo.
06:31 Priya: runtime behavior — once installed, how do you handle KV cache warm start? our concern is cold-start latency for the first requests after a restart.
06:40 Elena: great question. we support persistent KV cache snapshots. by default the runtime will write periodic KV checkpoints to disk. on restart it will warm the caches from the last checkpoint; for a faster warm start you can pre-populate the cache with a provided prefix snapshot. the checkpoint format is portable across our runtime versions in the same major line.
07:02 Priya: is that snapshot included in the offline bundle?
07:05 Elena: we can include an initial prefix snapshot for your common prompts; that will reduce first-token latency significantly. tradeoff: snapshot size vs coverage.
07:14 Liu: what about memory and disk sizing recommendations for the KV snapshots?
07:18 Elena: depends on sequence length and number of concurrent sessions. typical recommends: 16GB of reserved fast SSD per large-model instance for KV cache and checkpoint churn. we'll include a sizing table.
07:30 Marco: batching behavior — if the environment is strictly single-tenant, can we still do continuous batching?
07:36 Elena: yes, continuous batching works per node; if you run single-tenant and single-session you still get microbatching across concurrent requests. for very low-latency single-request scenarios you can set batch size 1 and pinned threads. we'll discuss autoscale policies offline.
07:52 Ethan: we care about deterministic latency. do you support fixed-time infer windows or do you have jitter from compilation?
07:59 Elena: the first request hitting a path that needs kernel JIT will have extra latency; we provide a compile-warm step during install to precompile kernels for expected shapes. also we have an autotune profile you can persist so subsequent restarts won't retrain.
08:20 Priya: quantization — we want to use int8 for cost savings but worried about eval regressions. how do you ship quantized kernels for an air-gapped environment?
08:31 Elena: we ship quantization profiles and the quantized kernels as part of the artifact. we'll run a recommended eval suite on your side. important note: some quantization techniques rely on CPU AVX512 or specific intrinsics; for non-x86 hosts or different CPU families you may see differences. we'll enumerate per-model caveats.
08:55 Tess: security detail — are any telemetry pings from runtime to Redwood? we must ensure none in production in the air-gapped footprint.
09:03 Jonah: by default telemetry is disabled in air-gapped bundles. if you enable it later we have an explicit opt-in installer flag that requires outbound connectivity. otherwise logs and metrics stay local; we provide a harvest-and-upload tool you run manually.
09:18 Marco: transfer mechanism question — we will likely use an internal transfer host to pull artifacts from our DMZ. will the signed manifest prevent tampering?
09:25 Jonah: yes, manifest is signed. additionally we include per-file sha256sums and a top-level signature. we can also provide signing keys for an internal verification step if you want to validate offline.
09:34 Ethan: benchmarking — what should we expect in terms of throughput for our RTX6000s at batch size 8 and sequence length 512? any ballpark numbers?
09:43 Elena: ballpark only: for a 70B-class model on an RTX6000 you might see ~8-12 tokens/sec depending on quantization and kernel path; with int8 quantization plus optimized kernels maybe 12-18. for A100s that jumps substantially. we'll include perf profiles per model/gpu in the artifact.
10:05 Priya: can you provide a small, automated benchmark harness as part of the bundle? we want reproducible numbers.
10:12 Elena: yes — a harness that runs a fixed prompt set, collects latency p50/p95/p99 and token throughput, and writes out structured CSVs. it runs offline and doesn't phone home.
10:21 Marco: for the kernel signatures: if we need to run signed kernel modules, what's the recommended process? we control the key for secure boot, right now we have secure boot on.
10:29 Elena: if secure boot is enabled you typically need signed modules with a key enrolled in the MOK. we can supply a module signed by NVIDIA or provide instructions to sign with your key; we can also provide a user-space only path. we'll document the secure-boot workflow.
10:46 Tess: one more on compliance — can we run a sample attestation report post-install? something like a hash of installed binaries plus manifest that we can keep?
10:55 Jonah: yes, installer emits an attestation bundle: sha256s of binaries, manifest, and a signature; we'll also provide a reproducible build provenance document.
11:08 Priya: ok let's recap the key deliverables and timeline.
11:12 Samir: deliverables = offline artifact tarball (split as needed) + OCI image tar + signed manifest/checksums, installer script with host checklist, offline activation instructions and token signing flow doc, benchmark harness, and perf profiles. we'll aim to get the initial bundle to you by 2025-02-19.
11:33 Marco: and we'll send you the host inventory and preferred transfer method by 2025-02-21.
11:38 Tess: security will review the offline activation flow doc; Samir you'll share the HSM key ownership statement?
11:44 Samir: yes I'll include a short doc describing HSM custody and issuance logs.
11:49 Priya: one open item: ROCm perf caveats — can you enumerate the model families and expected deltas in the docs?
11:56 Elena: will include a per-model ROCm note.
12:00 Samir: OK next steps in the calendar, action items recorded in the doc. any final questions?
12:06 Ethan: one small one — does the runtime support GPU isolation via MIG or MPS for mixed tenancy?
12:12 Elena: we support MIG on Ampere-class GPUs with caveats; MPS is supported for throughput scenarios; we'll include configuration examples.
12:22 Liu: thanks, that helps. looking forward to the bundle.
12:26 Samir: great, thanks everyone. we'll follow up with the artifact download instructions and the checklist. talk soon.

End of transcript.
